newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BUDAPEST GRAINS FUTURES RISE ON BAD WEATHER.
newsitem.headline: BUDAPEST GRAINS FUTURES RISE ON BAD WEATHER.

text.p: Grains futures continued their surge on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Tuesday on the combined effect on international prices and local cold weather, traders said.
"The weather is bad in some parts of the U.S. and western Europe, and in Hungary too, and markets reflect that," said Robert Vajo of Termin.
He added that current high prices suit both producers and buyers, thus trade has picked up for those months where the daily allowed movement limit has been lifted.
Milling wheat was only traded for freed-up October, December and March, and prices rose 700, 580 and 5,000 forints per tonne, respectively.
The limit on August feed wheat was also lifted and its price surged 3,200 forints to 25,500 forints, above August milling wheat which finished at 24,900 forints.
Maize went limit-up for all months but only saw significant trade for May, due to position-closing.
Feed barley prices went up 520 forints for July to 22,920 and 2,700 forints for September to 23,400.
Total grains turnover was 822.8 million forints or 1,609 contracts, with milling wheat accounting for 813 and maize for 399 lots.
